picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Pewter has allowed 120 points in nine games; Petalburg just won with fourteen. I expect the rested Rockers to turn that modest scoring appetite into a home upset, helped by the protection problems that produced three Pride sacks allowed.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Oinkologne's seventy-five rushing yards gave Norman a workable foundation against Viridian. I expect that foundation to keep Petalburg out of the obvious passing situations Pewter needs, while the Rockers' limited offense struggles to supply an answer.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Rockers have stayed involved in the season without asking their offense for much. I think the bye helps them find one extra useful possession against a Pride team that still has little margin when the passing game is quiet.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Seventy-seven points. In nine games. Petalburg does not need to stage an offensive revolution to beat that. I expect Norman's runners to provide enough support that Pewter cannot hide its scoring problem behind another respectable defensive afternoon.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Petalburg's recent rushing contribution offers the steadier way to maintain possession. Pewter can pressure the passer, but I expect the Pride to avoid enough long-yardage situations to finish one more scoring drive than the home offense.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Dewford needed overtime last time because it kept offering Viridian invitations. Celadon just threw for ninety-nine yards. I expect Ambipom to make the rested Breakers' next win considerably less dependent on an apology and a late kick.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Bloom stopped Mauville's running game and still lost by eighteen. I expect Dewford's ability to involve Ambipom in multiple ways to stretch that defensive workload further, without relying on one type of gain to sustain every drive.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Celadon has had a difficult stretch of disrupted personnel and incomplete offensive afternoons. I expect the rested Breakers' established contributors to make that uncertainty matter, even if Erika's runners keep the game competitive for a while.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Dewford's last win required a field goal with eight seconds left and overtime. That is not a royal procession. I expect Celadon's running game to keep the ball away, then another Breakers mistake to become the home team's opening.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Breakers have the broader recent offensive case, while Celadon's limited passing makes sustained scoring harder. I expect Dewford to gain enough from both Ambipom's rushing and receiving work to survive a few imperfect possessions.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Cerulean turned 251 passing yards into nine points and would like us to admire the yardage. I prefer Lavaridge's newly discovered habit of scoring touchdowns while allowing only seven. The Inferno get the upset until the Tide finish something.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Lavaridge's seven points allowed were useful, but Cerulean can challenge more of the field than Fuchsia finished last week. I expect Misty's passing game to find enough receiving opportunities to win, provided it gets even modest help on the ground.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Tide's two recent losses have exposed different problems, which makes a total collapse too simple a verdict. I expect a narrow home recovery against a defense whose improved latest game has not erased the longer record.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Nine points after fifty-six allowed the previous week. Cerulean is fixing one room while the next catches fire. I expect Delphox's careful passing to carry Lavaridge's improvement forward and force Misty to explain another unused collection of yards.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Cerulean still produced 251 passing yards at Fortree, and Lavaridge's broader defensive record remains vulnerable. I expect enough of that passing movement to become touchdowns at home, although the Tide's rushing weakness keeps the margin small.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Saffron sacked Marino four times without Brooks and came within three points of ruining Mossdeep's perfect record. Fortree has won three, which is charming. I expect the Psi Corps defense to make the fourth application considerably less enjoyable.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Skyhawks have used productive rushing to support Rabsca, but Saffron just held Mossdeep to ninety-six on the ground. I expect that front to make Fortree's passing downs more difficult than the recent winning streak has required.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Fortree's recovery deserves to be treated as real progress. I still expect Saffron's established defense to make the next step too large, especially if the Psi Corps turn their own 334-yard performance into cleaner possessions this time.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Winona has won three straight. Trent Scarboro has just watched a 17–6 lead disappear. I expect Fortree to carry its balance into this game while Saffron's mistakes leave the door open for a much louder fourth victory.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Psi Corps created pressure against a stronger offense than Fortree's recent opponents. I expect that disruption to limit Rabsca's comfortable completions, with Saffron's receivers producing enough scoring to turn a close loss into a home response.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Vermilion has six wins and a negative point differential, a balancing act I would not hire for children's parties. Its depleted secondary just allowed three touchdown passes without a sack. I expect Marino to make the same weakness expensive.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Dorrill's offense survived Saffron's pressure because it still had ways to finish. Vermilion produced no sack against Sootopolis and remains depleted at corner. I expect Mossdeep's receiving matchups to create separation before the Volts can exploit Flock's absence.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Mossdeep's narrow win showed an ability to stay involved when the early game was uncomfortable. I expect that patience to travel, while Vermilion's defensive absences make it difficult to protect a lead even if Chandelure starts well.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: I remain available to criticize Michael Dorrill. I am not obliged to pretend Vermilion's injured secondary is a convincing vehicle for it. Marino should find too many favorable throws, and the Eclipse should make this less dramatic than last week.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Volts' latest defense allowed efficient passing without generating pressure. I expect Mossdeep's passing game to exploit that combination, while its own remaining defenders do enough to keep Chandelure's response from matching a fuller Eclipse attack.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Drampa completed twenty of twenty-six without a sack or interception. Fuchsia answered its own manageable opponent with seven points. I expect Sootopolis to repeat enough of the clean passing to win, even if the Surge return to making it nervous.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Sootopolis has allowed 204 points, and one tidy passing day does not repair that defense. I expect Empoleon to turn his usual yardage into a few actual finishes against this opponent, while the Shadows finally make productive throws matter.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Fuchsia's record is bleak, but its passing game has kept producing opportunities that the endings have wasted. Against a Surge defense with a difficult season behind it, I think one of those afternoons finally reaches a better conclusion.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Empoleon threw for 212 yards and no touchdowns against Lavaridge. No touchdowns. I expect Drampa's cleaner finishing to expose the difference between moving the football and putting the opponent under actual scoring pressure. Sootopolis gets the points that matter.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Sootopolis' latest protection gave Drampa time to turn completions into three touchdowns. I expect that more complete offensive sequence to continue against Fuchsia, whose passing yards have too often stopped short of a comparable scoring return.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Furret had 137 receiving yards and Diggersby ran for seventy-seven. Oreburgh's useful parts are visible, even when the result is ugly. I expect fewer gifts this time and enough offense to punish an Azalea team still struggling to protect its passer.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Miners' interceptions keep undoing good rushing and receiving work. I expect Azalea's defense to create another short-field opportunity, and the Swarm's offense to recover enough against a less restrictive opponent than Eterna to use it.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Neither recent loss invites confidence. I give Azalea the smallest home edge because Oreburgh's recurring mistakes make its productive stretches harder to trust, while the Swarm should find more room than Eterna allowed them last week.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Oreburgh just allowed four touchdown passes on seventy-eight passing yards. That is a spectacularly poor exchange rate. I expect Azalea to take the opportunities the Miners keep offering and make its own limited offense look adequate for an afternoon.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Azalea should face less sustained pressure than Eterna applied, while Oreburgh's turnover pattern creates chances to shorten the field. I expect that combination to give the Swarm one more successful possession in an otherwise close game.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Eterna has finally brought an offense to its defensive meetings. Unfortunately, Mt. Silver just scored thirty-four while allowing nothing. I expect Tic Thorpe to create enough passing production that the Thorns need more than another useful Stantler afternoon.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Stantler gives Eterna a credible way to keep the game manageable, but Mt. Silver just paired clean possession management with productive third downs. I expect that passing consistency to force the Thorns beyond the scoring pace they prefer.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Thorns' defense has earned a proper examination against an unbeaten team. I think Stantler can preserve enough possession for it to provide one, and Eterna can win a game in which the Reds receive fewer convenient turnovers.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Connor McLarren's team won 34–0. Tic Thorpe accounted for four touchdowns. Eterna is a serious opponent, and the Reds will treat it seriously by scoring enough to make another excellent defensive afternoon insufficient. Nine unbeaten becomes ten.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Mt. Silver's latest offense converted seven of thirteen third downs without a turnover. I expect Eterna to reduce that efficiency but not eliminate it, while the Reds' defense makes the Thorns build more passing production than last week required.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Canalave lost four turnovers and scored zero, which is a very efficient way to look hopeless. I expect a cleaner afternoon to reveal a better team than that score, with Delcatty's pressure making Olivine's limited scoring cushion disappear.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Bulwark created three sacks and still produced only sixty-three passing yards. I expect Olivine to keep that passing game constrained, while Drampa's short, accurate work supplies enough possession to make Canalave's isolated pressures insufficient.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Olivine has answered its own shutout loss with two wins. I expect that steadier offense to hold up at home against a Canalave team still trying to reconnect defensive effort with offensive reward. The margin need not be large to be convincing.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Byron's team scored zero while Delcatty did enough rushing to collect three sacks. Reward the defense, for once. Until Canalave demonstrates that it can, I expect Olivine's recent habit of completing passes to produce the larger useful number.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Drampa's twenty-for-twenty-five performance offers Olivine a dependable way to sustain drives. Canalave's pressure should disrupt some possessions, but I expect its limited passing response to leave the home side with the extra touchdown it needs.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Four touchdowns on seventy-eight passing yards is not a ratio I would frame as a business plan. Swampert's ninety-two rushing yards are more reassuring. I expect that foundation to be enough against a Snowpoint offense fresh from zero points.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Cianwood can ask Swampert to carry more of the ordinary early-down work and keep Victreebel's passing decisions modest. I expect Snowpoint's limited rushing to make its own offense easier to contain, even without another extraordinary touchdown rate.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Crushers finally had an afternoon in which the available players could see their work become points. I expect that practical confidence, backed by Swampert's running, to survive a home game against a Blizzard team struggling to finish anything.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Seventy-eight passing yards will not normally buy four touchdowns. I expect Snowpoint to make Cianwood travel farther for its points, then discover enough offense against the Crushers to make last week's spectacular efficiency look like a temporary bargain.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Swampert provides Cianwood a more repeatable foundation than the four-touchdown passing line alone. I expect that running contribution to preserve enough scoring chances, while Snowpoint continues struggling to support its passing game with useful rushing.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Violet has won three straight by making other offenses equally uncomfortable. Hearthome just made Blackthorn sweat, but I expect the Falcons' repeated defensive resistance to matter more than another Haunts argument that the loss was almost impressive.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Hearthome produced 217 passing yards and two passing touchdowns against Blackthorn without allowing a sack. I expect that protection to make Violet work harder than its recent opponents did, with Frosmoth supplying enough scoring to overturn a small home edge.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Haunts keep showing more usable offense than their record advertises. I think that progress can survive this trip, and Violet's small scoring margins leave room for the visitor's latest passing improvement to become a win instead of another near miss.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Violet's latest opponent scored six. Hearthome's latest opponent scored twenty-seven. I expect the Falcons to keep this in their preferred neighborhood, then force Fantina's team to explain another close result without receiving another victory.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Violet has repeated its ability to limit offensive finishing, while Hearthome still carries important absences. I expect the Falcons to reduce the Haunts' recent passing efficiency enough that one extra home touchdown decides a narrow game.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Lavender completed nine passes; Veilstone threw two interceptions. Selecting a winner should come with a folding chair and a long sigh. I expect the Wails' earlier receiving production to reappear just often enough to survive at home.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Lavender's only touchdown last week came on a punt return, and its offense converted one of nine third downs. I expect Veilstone's defense to sustain that discomfort, while the Fists protect the ball just well enough to win a modest scoring exchange.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Wails' recent collapse is real, but the receiving group's better afternoons were real too. I expect a home response against another limited offense, with enough sustained possessions to let the defense protect something other than a special-teams rescue.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Nine completions. Ninety-six yards. Travis Scarboro cannot keep asking us to remember the good stretches while the present offense disappears. I expect Veilstone's pressure and a more careful Tatsugiri to turn Lavender's current problem into another loss.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Lavender has shown more offensive range earlier in the season than Veilstone's recent attack. I expect a limited recovery at home, with the Wails finding enough completions to edge an opponent that still struggles to finish possessions without turnovers.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Mahogany's positive differential has been requesting a better record for weeks. Pastoria just found a competent passing afternoon, but I expect the rested Frost to make that improvement less comfortable on the road and finally keep a complete win.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Pastoria ran for forty-two yards against Lavender, leaving its passing game to carry most of the scoring work. I expect Mahogany to make that imbalance harder to sustain, with the home offense taking enough possession to control a close result.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Frost's season has contained more competitive football than its three wins suggest. I expect the bye to help turn that into a proper result, even against a Pastoria team whose passing revival deserves to be taken seriously.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Pastoria scored seventeen and would now like a parade for completing the assignment. Mahogany has a stronger season-long scoring balance. I expect the Frost to make the Waves earn longer drives, then finish enough of their own to settle it.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Mahogany's stronger scoring balance and home advantage outweigh Pastoria's single improved passing result for me. I expect the Frost to keep the Waves' rushing limited, forcing enough difficult passing possessions to preserve a one-score advantage.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Blackthorn is 8–1, and Hatterene just completed seventeen of twenty-one. Sunyshore has had a week to rest and remain irritating. I expect the Dragons' passing efficiency to make the visitors pay for the few possessions their running game cannot protect.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Hearthome held Blackthorn to forty-nine rushing yards and still nearly won the passing exchange. I expect Sunyshore's more balanced recent offense to keep Hatterene waiting, then create enough scoring chances to justify the difficult road pick.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Dragons escaped by two while the Starseekers had time to prepare. I think Sunyshore's useful rushing response at Lavender can travel, giving the visitors the patient possessions needed to win without pretending Hatterene will suddenly become careless.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Hatterene has supplied another efficient win, and Clair's team is 8–1. Sunyshore's bye does not come with points attached. I expect Blackthorn's passing to make the Starseekers chase the game, then force the road offense into the less comfortable choices.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Sunyshore's latest balance gives it a narrow route to controlling possession against a Blackthorn team that just struggled to run. I expect enough of that rushing support to survive the trip and create one more decisive scoring opportunity.

recordMethod: Straight-up winner, actual ties separately. Closest score uses abs(predicted away - actual away) + abs(predicted home - actual home). Every panelist tied for lowest error gets one shared closest bonus; bonuses are independent of correct winner and do not alter the W-L record.
